messages:
ana: Quick sync — I put together a minimal set of launch gates for the tool-calling + structured-output push. Need to lock acceptance criteria and edge-case behavior by EOD Fri. :calendar:

mike (SWE): can you paste the high-level gates? I can start filling defs for infra and rollout steps. :+1:

ana (PM): sure — high level: 1) JSON-schema validation pass rate >= 99.5% on canary prompt set, 2) end-to-end tool success rate >= 99% (excluding downstream third-party errors), 3) clear fallback path w/ documented UX, 4) observability: per-route schema_failure and tool_call_latency metrics, 5) rollout plan with 0.5/1/5/20/100% steps and automated rollback on regression.

kim (ML Eng): for schema pass rate, do we count "fixable" type coercions (e.g., string->int) as pass? we see lots of model-y casts.

ana (PM): good q. proposal: allow benign coercions by canonicalizer only if we can auto-transform without losing semantics. Record them separately as schema_coercion events, but still count as pass. If canonicalizer modifies semantics (e.g., truncate arrays), count as failure.

jordan (ProdDesign): UX note — fallback to plain text should include a short explainer and a suggestion to try again with "structured: relax" flag. We should surface that fallback reason code in the response so client can choose UI.

mike (SWE): sketch of error response we can standardize (json):
```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "TOOL_UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "Tool 'price_lookup' returned 5xx",
    "fallback": true,
    "hint": "try_again_or_use_model_variant"
  }
}
```

mike (SWE): also propose header X-Redwood-Validation: pass|coerce|fail so infra can route logs quickly.

sam (EngInfra): +1. We need telemetry names and suggested tags now so we can add to dashboards: redwood.tool_call.success, redwood.tool_call.failure.{reason}, redwood.schema.validation.{pass,coerce,fail}. Tags: route, model_version, customer_tier, canary_id.

kim (ML Eng): edge cases to add to acceptance tests: - ambiguous tool selection (two tools match) - model returns additional unexpected keys - truncated arrays (partial outputs) - nested objects with mismatched types - streaming tool calls that timeout mid-stream

ana (PM): for ambiguous tool selection: acceptance criteria = model_confidence_delta >= 0.15 between top-1 and top-2 OR system ties break to explicit tool preference list. If both fail, treat as validation fail -> fallback. Document in spec.

mike (SWE): streaming timeouts: plan to add a strong TTL and a circuit-breaker. If tool stream dies, runtime should return partial structured payload + "incomplete": true and include the tool error block above. Client gets 206-like semantic.

jordan (ProdDesign): UI should treat incomplete structured payloads as lower confidence; show "partial" badge and allow manual retry.

ana (PM): rollout plan: canary 5% for 24h on internal customers + synthetic prompt set (500 prompts): require schema_pass >= 99% and tool_success >= 99.5%. If either drops by >0.5% absolute vs baseline, auto-roll back. After 24h, expand to 25% for 48h, then 100% if green.

sam (EngInfra): infra tasks: create feature-flag gate, add canary_id header, bootstrap dashboards, implement automated rollback hook tied to baseline metrics. I’ll open infra tickets after this thread.

mike (SWE): acceptance criteria checklist I’ll add to PRD: - schema validator integrated in runtime - canonicalizer rules documented + test vectors - fallback error schema implemented - headers and telemetry in place - canary feature flag + rollback automation - integration tests for listed edge cases

kim (ML Eng): test vectors: I’ll assemble 200 prompts covering nested structures, optional fields, and intentional noise. Will surface a few failing examples today.

ana (PM): thanks. small decision: do we require model to emit schema version metadata? I think yes — "schema_version" field on responses so we can evolve schemas without ambiguity.

mike (SWE): agreed. runtime will validate schema_version against model_claimed_schema. If missing, treat as coercion/fail depending on content.

ops-bot: Created checklist: CH-4821 (schema validator), CH-4822 (fallback format), CH-4823 (telemetry tags), CH-4824 (canary automation).

jordan (ProdDesign): can we add a short guidance doc for customers on how to handle fallback UX? I'll draft a 1-pager.

ana (PM): yes — include examples: 1) full success, 2) coercion-only, 3) partial output, 4) tool-unavailable. Each example shows sample response and recommended UI copy.

mike (SWE): one more edgecase: when model emits valid schema but semantic values are nonsense (e.g., negative price). How strict do we want semantic checks?

kim (ML Eng): recommend lightweight semantic validators in pipeline configurable per-route (e.g., min/max, enums). Flag semantic_violations but don't auto-fail unless configured. Record metric redwood.schema.semantic_violation.

ana (PM): wrap-up: Mike/Kim/Sam — action items: write acceptance criteria into PRD, add test vectors, and list infra tickets by EOD Thu. Jordan: UX 1-pager by Mon. I’ll consolidate and schedule a 30m review Fri 10:30am. :calendar: :eyes:

mike (SWE): got it.

kim (ML Eng): on it.

sam (EngInfra): will queue infra work.

jordan (ProdDesign): drafting.

ana (PM): thanks team.
